lines.text: Another Sworn, fresh off the forge-table. Steel in your bones and Midgard in your blood. Welcome to Gladsheim.
No time for songs. The heat-lines from Nidavellir have gone cold. Midgard is freezing from the outer wall inward.
Something in the Iron Wood is cutting them. The gate will take you there. Find it, and stop it.
Brokkr will arm you, the rune-carver will sharpen what he makes, and the board has work if you want charms. Mind the Valkyries: they carry the fallen home, and they keep a toll.
The heat-line runs through here. It's been torn open, not worn through.
Rime-engines and thralls by the dozen. Something drove them south. Keep moving north and you'll find what.
Feel that wind? The Fimbulwinter surges here. Stand near a burning brazier when it comes, or it will freeze you where you stand.
Unlit braziers take a spark: a shot, a burning blow, or your own hand.
A Well of Wyrd. The Norns keep one rule in each. Here: nothing touching the ground can be hurt.
Lift them, then cut them down. Win, and the well gives a sigil and whatever it keeps.
Bones and slag, and something heavy breathing in the dark.
An iron troll. Break its legs and it kneels; climb it then. Break its arms and it stops throwing.
Its last swipe splits your plating and finds the flesh beneath. Cold pours in.
Come home, Sworn. My well can mend you as you were: quicker, and still flesh. Or Brokkr can mend you as you could be: steel, and heavier for it.
Come to the well when you are ready to choose. Either way, the well remembers, and you may choose again.
Flesh remembers. You will be faster for it, and you will bleed for it. Go well.
The cut came from the forges themselves. Nidavellir. The gate is open to it now.
There. Steel doesn't feel cold and doesn't feel fear. Hit harder. Try not to forget why.
The cut came from the forges themselves. Nidavellir. The gate is open to it now.
Nidavellir. The forges that keep Midgard alive, and every one of them banked cold.
The conveyors still run. Use them, or be carried by them. Somewhere below, someone is drawing the heat off.
My vents! Still blowing on a cycle. Stand clear when they rumble.
Or don't stand clear: put the rime-engines on them. Launch them right into the fire. I'd enjoy that.
lines.human: Or put the rime-engines on them. You're quick enough to launch them right into the fire.
lines.cyber: Or put the rime-engines on them. You're heavy enough now to throw them in.

lines.text: The high way. Narrow and fast, over the drop. Flesh is light enough to cross it. Knock them off; don't follow.
The smelter floor. Heavy enough to hold you, now. See those pylons? They're shielding the bulwarks. Smash the pylons first.
The Well of the Mark. Here nothing can be hurt unless it already suffers: burning, freezing, shocked or bound.
Your blows can still mark them, if your runes or your skills carry a status. Then strike.
The forge-heart. Something has threaded a channel through it, and the heat runs down, not out.
Down. Toward Hvergelmir. Who drinks from a spring of fire?
The forge-heart burns again. Midgard's outer wall will thaw by morning.
But the channel goes on down, to the roots and the boiling spring. Whatever cut the heat-lines is drinking at Hvergelmir.
Old songs say a giant of stone once came to Asgard to drink and boast. They say its heart was a whetstone. I hope the songs are wrong.
Ice, and under it, black water that steams where it touches the air.
Thin ice. Heavy blows will crack it, and what's cracked gives way. Use it, but don't stand on it when it goes.
The geysers throw anything standing near them into the air. Lure foes over them and you'll have them where you want them.
The Well of Standing. No dodging here. Read their blows, keep your distance, and strike in the gaps.
Beyond this gate the spring boils, and something vast is breathing.
Whatever you find, Sworn, you were made for this, flesh or steel.
The caldera. Something vast stands in the spring, drinking its heat.
Stone, from horn to heel. And beside it a thing of clay, patting mud onto its master's plates.
Hrungnir, and his clay-son. Stop the mending, Sworn, or every blow you land is wasted on stone.
lines.human: Hrungnir, and his clay-son. Stop the mending, Sworn. Flesh tires; spend it where it counts.
lines.cyber: Hrungnir, and his clay-son. Stop the mending, Sworn. Brokkr's steel will hold if you aim it.

lines.text: The stone heart cracks. Heat floods back into the roots. I can feel the heat-lines waking, one by one.
The forges are burning again. From the outer wall inward, the frost is giving ground.
You were made for this, flesh or steel.
lines.human: You kept your own heart and still broke a stone one. Remember that.
lines.cyber: Brokkr's steel held. He will be unbearable about it.

lines.text: Listen, though. Under the ice, the spring still hums. The giants Hrungnir meant to wake are sleeping. Not gone. Sleeping.
Then I'll end the song there: the winter breaks, the giants sleep, and the Sworn come home. Chapter one.
The stone remembers me. So do I.
